text:
Nora (People Ops): Quick update for distributed teams: we're standardizing PTO accrual and carryover rules to align with local employment laws and simplify reporting. Effective 2026-08-01. Policy doc: https://redwood.atlassian.org/people-ops/leave/global-accrual-2026 

HR-Compliance-Bot: New policy published. Highlights: country-specific accrual caps, pro-rated start-date accrual for new hires, and automatic carryover limits set per local regulation. 

Liam Ortega: Can you summarize what changes for EU vs US employees?

Nora (People Ops): Short summary: US: unchanged for exempt full-time (accrual cadence monthly), carryover cap tightened to 40 hours for non-exempt exemptions; EU & UK: we've adjusted to meet statutory minimums and local holiday integration (some countries require calendar-year reset). Full table in the doc. 

Chen Wei: I'm in Singapore — does this affect my accrual rate or existing bank?

Nora (People Ops): For Singapore, accrual moves to statutory minimum if company policy previously exceeded it; existing balances are grandfathered but new accrual follows local cadence. We added a one-time adjustment window (submit within 60 days) if you think your balance was miscalculated. 

Liam Ortega: What about part-time or contractor conversions? My team just moved a 0.6 FTE to 0.8 FTE. 

Nora (People Ops): Accrual will be pro-rated by FTE as of the effective date. If someone's FTE changed mid-pay-period, we'll pro-rate for that month. Contractors who convert to employees will start prorated accrual from their first day as an employee. 

HR-Compliance-Bot: Managers: when approving PTO requests during the transition window (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-15), please confirm current balances in Workday and flag discrepancies to People-ops-Support. 

Chen Wei: Any retroactive adjustments for recent leave taken? I had a long leave in May.

Nora (People Ops): Retroactive adjustments are limited: we will correct clear calculation errors and honor statutory protections. For discretionary retro pay or reinstatement of hours, submit a ticket to people-ops@redwood.com with subject "Accrual Review" and include payroll dates. 

Liam Ortega: Carryover specifics? We have folks in APAC saving PTO for travel. 

Nora (People Ops): Carryover rules now follow local limits. Where the law allows carryover, we cap at either the statutory limit or 1.5x annual accrual, whichever is lower. In countries that require use-or-lose, we'll notify employees 60 days before year-end and offer time-off planning assistance. 

People-ops-Support: FYI: We'll run an employee balance export next week and send personal notices to anyone affected. Expect an inbox item "Action needed: PTO balance update" if you need to submit documentation. 

Chen Wei: Will managers need to approve any forced time-off to comply with local rules?

Nora (People Ops): In some jurisdictions, yes. We'll work with managers before any forced scheduling. People-ops will propose dates and provide coverage suggestions. Managers should coordinate with their teams and cc people-ops. 

Liam Ortega: Payroll impact? Will this change accrual on pay statements?

Nora (People Ops): Payroll changes will be reflected starting the first payroll after 2026-08-01. If you see a discrepancy, report to payroll@redwood.com with "PTO Accrual Discrepancy". 

HR-Compliance-Bot: Reminder: employees in countries with statutory notice requirements will receive localized guidance and a consent form where required. 

Chen Wei: Any office hours to walk through examples?

Nora (People Ops): Yes 15-min drop-in sessions next Wed 08:00 PT and Thu 16:00 PT in #people-ops-office-hours. I'll post example scenarios in the doc (US, UK, SG, DE). Also running manager-only Q&A Friday 09:00 PT. 

Liam Ortega: Thanks Nora. Appreciate the heads-up.

People-ops-Support: We'll send personalized messages to impacted employees by next Tuesday. Ping us for escalations.

Nora (People Ops): Thanks all 44d. Please read the policy and reach out if you need help with a specific case.
